name: Agents behind worker
summary: Agents run on an internal-only network whose only route out is a Warden worker. Recipes ship for Ethos, Hermes, OpenClaw and ZeroClaw.

name: Identity contract + CLI
label: identity-contract
summary: Defines how any agent platform sends a user's identity to Warden and ships a small `warden identity` CLI so any agent, script or harness can get a token and route through the worker. Warden stays platform-neutral: a harness only needs an OIDC token from the configured issuer and a proxy URL.
design: Contract: an OIDC ID token from the configured issuer with `aud` containing `warden`, `exp` at most 1h out, and a `groups` claim. With Dex this is obtained through cross-client trust (`audience:server:client_id:warden` scope on the `agent-harness` client).

Transport: `Proxy-Authorization: Basic base64("session:"+token)` on CONNECT, which any client gets from a proxy URL `http://session:<token>@worker:8080`. Fallback header `X-Warden-Identity: Bearer <token>` on requests Warden terminates. Both are stripped before forwarding.
Harness duties: refresh before expiry, give each user's processes only that user's token, and never place the token in model context, prompts, logs or tool output.

`warden identity` CLI (new package internal/identityclient): `login` runs the OIDC device-code flow against the configured issuer and stores the refresh token in a 0600 file; `token` prints a valid ID token, refreshing at 2/3 lifetime; `env` prints HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY with the session credentials for the given worker.
Phase 2 extends the same package with agent keys and RFC 8693 token exchange, so platforms that adopt the CLI or contract upgrade without rework.
done_when: A plain curl container with no agent framework gets a token with `warden identity`, sends requests through the worker, and every event in the CP dashboard carries that user's sub, email and groups.

name: Identity client + recipes
label: identity-client

summary: Ship a reference Dex deployment that Warden and any agent harness trust: one IdP fronting the company directory, issuing short-lived ID tokens with groups. Operators get a pinned, documented compose recipe and config they can point at LDAP/GitHub/Google connectors. Warden treats Dex only as a generic OIDC issuer.
design: Static clients: `warden` is confidential, with redirectURIs `<cp>/auth/callback` and `trustedPeers: [agent-harness]`. `agent-harness` is a generic client for agent platforms and the `warden identity` CLI, with device-code enabled and redirectURIs `<harness>/auth/callback`. Secrets come from env (`$WARDEN_DEX_CLIENT_SECRET`, `$HARNESS_DEX_CLIENT_SECRET`) and are never committed.

`expiry.idTokens: 1h`, `expiry.signingKeys: 6h`, and refresh tokens with `validIfNotUsedFor: 168h` and `absoluteLifetime: 720h`. Storage is sqlite3 on a named volume. The groups claim comes from the connector.

The dev recipe uses an OpenLDAP container seeded with users and groups (warden-admins, warden-editors, warden-viewers, eng). Dex static passwords are not a reliable source of the groups claim, so they are not used for role tests. Commented examples cover the GitHub (orgs/teams), Google and generic OIDC connectors.
Pin the image to an exact released tag by digest, e.g. `ghcr.io/dexidp/dex:v2.x.y@sha256:...`, chosen at implementation time from the latest stable release that is at least 2 weeks old.

Issuer URL consistency: the issuer must be byte-identical for browsers and containers. The recipe uses `http://dex:5556/dex` and documents a hosts entry for local runs. The production docs require https.
done_when: `docker compose -f deploy/compose/docker-compose.identity.yml up` brings up Dex + LDAP, and a seeded user can obtain an ID token with aud=warden, a groups claim and exp-iat=3600.

name: Dex (one IdP)
label: dex-oidc

summary: Employees sign in to the consent portal on the CP with their Dex identity, using a session type separate from the admin console and with no console privileges. The login requests offline_access so the CP holds each user's Dex refresh token, which offboarding later uses to detect disabled users.
design: Separate OIDC client registration (config consent.oidc: issuer, clientID, clientSecretEnv, redirectURL=/portal/callback, scopes [openid,email,profile,groups,offline_access]) reusing the generic OIDC client code from p1-sso-roles; no Dex-specific calls.

Session type portal: cookie __Host-warden_portal (Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/), server-side row in CP SQLite table portal_sessions(id_hash, sub, email, created_at, expires_at, last_seen_at); idle timeout consent.session.idle (default 30m), absolute lifetime consent.session.max (default 8h). Portal sessions are rejected by all /dashboard/api/* handlers and vice versa.

Dex refresh token stored in the secret backend at warden/users/<sub>/_idp (never in SQLite); table idp_links(sub, email, refresh_ref, linked_at, last_refresh_at, last_refresh_status) holds only a Reference.
CSRF: double-submit token bound to the session (X-CSRF-Token header required on every non-GET /portal/api/* call); auth code flow uses state + nonce + PKCE S256 with a 10-minute pending login record.
Logout deletes the session row; it does not delete the stored refresh token (offboarding still needs it).
done_when: An employee in Dex can sign in at /portal, gets a portal session that cannot call any console API, and their Dex refresh token is in the secret backend at warden/users/<sub>/_idp.

name: Consent sign-in
label: consent-auth

summary: Warden resolves a person's groups directly from Okta, Microsoft Entra ID or Google Workspace, so Dex becomes optional. The console, worker identity verification and token service accept ID tokens from one or more configured issuers, and group lookups that the token cannot carry (Entra overage, Google) go through a cached directory adapter.
design: New package internal/idp with `type GroupResolver interface { Groups(ctx context.Context, iss, sub string, claims map[string]any) ([]string, error) }` and adapters `claims` (read a configured claim, default `groups`), `okta`, `entra`, `google`; Dex keeps using the `claims` adapter.

Multi-issuer config block `identity.issuers[]: {name, issuer, clientID, audiences[], groupSource: claims|okta|entra|google, groupsClaim, cacheTTL}`; the OIDC verifier from p1-verify-token becomes a map keyed by `iss`, each with its own JWKS cache; unknown `iss` is rejected (401), never falls through to another issuer.

Entra: if the token has `_claim_names.groups` / `hasgroups` (overage), call Microsoft Graph `POST /v1.0/users/{oid}/getMemberGroups` with app-only client credentials (`clientSecretEnv` or certificate); group IDs are mapped to display names only if `entra.resolveNames: true`. Okta: `groups` claim from a custom authorization server, optional `GET /api/v1/users/{id}/groups` fallback with an SSWS token from env.

Google: Admin SDK Directory API `groups.list?userKey=<email>` using a service account with domain-wide delegation (`google.serviceAccountKeyEnv`, `google.adminSubject`); Google ID tokens carry no groups, so this path is mandatory for Google.

Resolved groups are cached per (iss, sub) for `cacheTTL` (default 10m) with singleflight; on directory API failure the cached value is used up to `staleTTL`, after which role mapping yields no groups (viewer-or-deny, never a widened role). Directory credentials are fetched via internal/secrets and never written to CP state.
Group strings are namespaced `<issuer-name>:<group>` only when more than one issuer is configured, so p1-sso-roles mappings and p1-group-policy rules stay unambiguous.
done_when: With Dex removed from the compose stack, a user signing in through Okta, Entra (including an overage account) or Google gets the correct console role and group-based policy on the worker.

name: Fleet dashboard
summary: Fleet dashboard on the control plane with per-worker slicing, a live policy editor, MCP inventory per worker, alerts and Explore.

The control-plane console becomes an OIDC client of Dex. Humans sign in with auth code + PKCE, get a server-side session, and are mapped from IdP groups to admin, editor or viewer. Every dashboard write API checks the role. The shared bearer token stops working for human endpoints.
design: New package `internal/cpstate`: one SQLite DB `<state-dir>/warden-cp.db` (modernc.org/sqlite, already a dependency) with a forward-only `schema_migrations` table. It holds sessions and the stores that later items add (versions, tokens, admin audit, block list). OIDC console mode requires `--state-dir`.

CP-local config block `console:` (json:"-", never on the policy wire): `auth: none|oidc`, `oidc: {issuer, clientID, clientSecretEnv, redirectURL, scopes}`, `roles: {admin: [groups], editor: [groups], viewer: [groups]}`, `session: {idle: 8h, absolute: 24h}`. The highest matching role wins, and no match means 403 after login.

Routes on the CP mux: `GET /auth/login` (state, nonce, S256 PKCE verifier kept in a cpstate `oidc_pending` row with 10 min TTL), `GET /auth/callback` (code exchange via golang.org/x/oauth2, ID token verified with the internal/identity verifier using aud=clientID, nonce checked), `POST /auth/logout`, and `GET /auth/me`.

Session cookie `warden_session`: 32 random bytes, stored as a sha256 hash, HttpOnly, Secure (when TLS), SameSite=Lax. A per-session CSRF token must be echoed in `X-Warden-CSRF` on every non-GET request.

Authz middleware wraps `dash.Handler()` and `/central/secrets` with a route table (method+path -> minimum role). GET is viewer. Policy/settings/detection writes are editor. Integrations, llmproviders, secrets, worker tokens and the block list are admin. A mutating route missing from the table is denied.

`console.auth: none` keeps today's open dashboard for back-compat, but logs a startup warning and shows a banner. In `oidc` mode the shared token is rejected on `/central/secrets` and all `/dashboard/*` routes.
done_when: With `console.auth: oidc`, an LDAP user in warden-viewers can read but gets 403 on POST /dashboard/api/policy, a warden-editors user can edit policy, only warden-admins can edit integrations, and the WARDEN_CP_TOKEN bearer no longer opens any dashboard or /central/secrets route.

summary: Every change made through the CP console or API is recorded with who did it, what changed, and the state hashes before and after. summary: Policy and distributed settings move from in-place edits of the served YAML into a versioned store in CP state. Every save creates a new immutable version with author and message, admins can diff any two versions and roll back in one click, and workers are always served the current version. Existing deployments migrate automatically on first start.
design: cpstate table `policy_versions(version INTEGER PK, created_at, author_sub, author_email, message, parent_version, doc_json, doc_sha256)`, where doc_json is the policyWire body {allowlist, denylist, settings}, and a `policy_head(version)` pointer. Versions are append-only.
Rollback to version N creates version M = latest+1 with N's doc and message `rollback to N`. History is never rewritten. `blockedUsers` lives outside versions, so a rollback can never unblock a user.

`policyServer.loadPolicy` reads the head version from the store instead of the YAML file. The ETag stays the sha256 prefix of the marshaled wire, so long-poll and the worker `behind` flag work unchanged.

`WritePolicy`/`WriteSettings` (ConfigEditor) create a version and require `If-Match: <head version>`, returning 409 on a stale head. CP-local blocks (integrations, detection, console) stay in the served YAML and keep today's YAML round-trip editor.

Migration: if the store is empty at start, import the current served config's policy+settings as version 1 (author `import`). After that, external edits of `policy:`/settings blocks in the YAML are ignored with a warning, and `warden policy import --state-dir <dir> --file <yaml> --message` creates a version from a file.
Diff: structural, not textual. Allow/deny entries are keyed by domain+port+groups (added/removed/changed), and settings by JSON path.
done_when: An editor saves three policy changes, sees three versions with author and diffs, rolls back to version 1, and workers pull the rolled-back policy within one long-poll cycle, with each step recorded in the admin audit log.

summary: Admins can block a person by Dex sub or email from the console. The list ships to workers inside the policy wire type as `blockedUsers`, and workers deny any request whose verified identity matches, within one long-poll cycle. This is the P1 offboarding and incident kill switch.

Worker match: sub exact match, or email case-insensitive match against the verified identity. Checked at CONNECT when Proxy-Authorization identity is present, and again for each request in the new identity stage, so kept-alive TLS sessions are cut on the next request.

summary: Adds a signing-key subsystem to the control plane that owns every key the CP signs with (Warden tokens, policy bundles). Keys carry a kid, rotate on a schedule with an overlap window, and are published as a JWKS so workers and harnesses can verify without a shared secret.

Supported algs: EdDSA (Ed25519, default) and ES256; kid = base64url(SHA-256(JWK thumbprint, RFC 7638)).

Private keys stored through the existing secrets.SecretStore (Put/Get) under `warden/cp/keys/<purpose>/<kid>`; CP SQLite stores only metadata (kid, alg, purpose, state active|next|retired, created_at, activates_at, retires_at).

summary: Replaces per-worker bearer tokens with short-lived mTLS client certificates issued by a CP-held intermediate CA. Workers enroll once with a single-use token, then renew automatically; operators revoke a worker by revoking its cert.
design: CP intermediate CA: key stored via secrets.SecretStore (`warden/cp/ca/intermediate`), cert chain configured by `workerCA.certFile` (operator signs it offline from their root, or `proxy control-plane ca init` creates a self-signed root+intermediate for dev).

Enrollment: admin creates a single-use token (random 32 bytes, stored hashed, TTL 1h, bound to a worker id) in the console; worker calls `POST /enroll` with token + CSR (ECDSA P-256), gets a 24h cert with URI SAN `spiffe://<trust-domain>/warden/worker/<id>`, ExtKeyUsage clientAuth.
Renewal: `POST /enroll/renew` authenticated by the current cert, new CSR, at 2/3 lifetime (16h); expired cert requires re-enrollment.

CP TLS listener uses tls.VerifyClientCertIfGiven with the intermediate pool; /policy, /control/heartbeat, /central/ingest, /central/secrets require a verified worker cert whose SPIFFE id is not revoked; the console and /oauth2/token stay cookie/assertion-authenticated.
Revocation: `worker_certs` table (serial, worker id, not_after, revoked_at); revoked serials (unexpired only) shipped in the signed bundle and checked by CP on every request.
Per-worker tokens from P1 accepted only while `workerAuth.legacyTokens: true` (default false after migration), then removed.
done_when: A fresh worker enrolls with a one-time token, runs for over 24h renewing automatically, is cut off within one request after its cert is revoked, and per-worker tokens are disabled.

summary: The CP signs everything it ships to workers as one canonical bundle, and workers verify it against a pinned key before applying. A compromised network path or CP replica serving stale or forged policy can no longer change worker behavior.
design: Bundle JSON: {version (monotonic int from policy history), issuedAt, policy (existing policyWire incl. settings and agents), blockedUsers, jwks (token keys), revocations (worker cert serials)}; canonicalized with RFC 8785 JCS before signing.

Envelope served on existing `GET /policy`: {bundle, sig: base64url Ed25519, kid}; ETag = version; served only when `bundles.signed: true` (default true once rolled out), plain wire kept for local-only and old workers behind `bundles.legacyUnsigned`.

Signing key from internal/keys with purpose=bundle (separate from token keys); worker pins bundle public keys via config `controlPlane.bundleKeys` (list of JWK or file) and accepts any listed kid, allowing pinned rotation.

Worker rejects: missing/invalid sig, unknown kid, version < last applied (rollback), issuedAt more than 5m in the future; on reject keeps last-known-good, logs, increments `warden_bundle_rejected_total{reason}`, and reports the rejection in heartbeat.
Last-known-good bundle persisted to the worker state dir (envelope + sig) so restarts re-verify and resume without the CP; fail-closed behavior until first valid bundle is preserved.

summary: Policy changes go through draft, pending and approved states, and changes that widen what agents can do need a second person. Before approving, reviewers see a replay of recent traffic against the draft showing which requests would newly be allowed or denied.
design: Tables `policy_drafts` (id, base_version, author, state draft|pending|approved|rejected|applied, body YAML, created_at) and `policy_approvals` (draft_id, approver, decision, comment, at); approval of a draft creates a new version in P1 policy history; base_version mismatch at apply time forces rebase.

Widening detection in new package internal/approvals: compare base and draft config.Policy; widening = new or broadened allowlist entry (wildcard/regex broadening, new methods/ports), removed denylist entry, removed blockedUsers, relaxed rate limit or time window, identity mode lowered, agent allowed_groups added.

summary: A small employee-facing UI on the CP at /portal lists connected accounts, lets the user connect or revoke a provider and shows which agents used each grant recently. It also hosts the landing page for a pending authorization created by a JIT 403.

summary: A CP background job refreshes each user's stored Dex refresh token on a schedule; when Dex refuses it or reports the user disabled, the user is blocked and all their provider grants are revoked and deleted. Admins can also offboard a user manually from the console.
design: Job: every consent.offboarding.interval (default 1h, jittered), for each idp_links row refresh at the Dex token endpoint with grant_type=refresh_token; store the rotated refresh token back to warden/users/<sub>/_idp; record last_refresh_status.

Failure classes: invalid_grant (user disabled, deleted or session revoked in the upstream IdP) → offboard; network/5xx → retry with backoff, alert after consent.offboarding.maxFailures (default 3) consecutive transient failures, never offboard on transient errors.

Offboard(sub, reason): add sub to blockedUsers in the current policy version (p1-block-list) first, then for each grant RevokeUserGrant, then delete warden/users/<sub>/_idp and mark idp_links offboarded; idempotent and resumable.
Manual: POST /dashboard/api/users/{sub}/offboard (admin role) with reason; audit user.offboarded with actor, reason and the list of revoked providers; alert routed through internal/alertpipeline.
done_when: Disabling a user in Dex results, within one job interval, in that user being on the block list, their provider tokens revoked at the provider and their vault entries deleted, with an audit record.

summary: Users approve delegation grants that let a specific agent act for them for a stated purpose, with a fixed tool set and expiry. The token service issues tokens carrying `grant_id`, the worker limits MCP tools to the grant's tool set, and users or admins can revoke grants at any time with immediate effect.
design: New package internal/grants with a SQLite table `grants` in CP state: id (`grt_` + 128-bit random), sub, agent_id, purpose, tools (JSON array, namespaced `server__tool` or bare tool), providers/scopes, expires_at, status `pending|active|denied|revoked|expired`, created_at, approved_at, revoked_at, revoked_by, revoke_reason.

Agents request via `POST /api/grants` (agent private_key_jwt assertion + user ID token as subject); requested tools must be a subset of the agent's policy-allowed tools and expiry is capped by `grants.maxTTL` (default 30d, per-agent override). Response: {grant_id, approve_url, status_url}.
Consent portal page `/portal/grants/{id}`: only the grant's sub can act; the user can deselect tools and shorten expiry but never add; approve/deny with CSRF token.

Token service accepts `subject_token_type=urn:warden:params:token-type:grant`; validates active, unexpired, agent match; issues JWT with `grant_id`, `tools` claim, sub=user, act.sub=agent, exp=min(15m, grant expiry).

Worker: MCP `tools/call` with a grant token must name a tool in the `tools` claim (intersection with policy, never a union), otherwise Deny with reason `mcp_grant_scope`. Revoked grant ids ride the signed bundle (`revokedGrants`) so outstanding tokens die on next bundle apply.
Every lifecycle change (request, approve, narrow, deny, revoke, expire) writes an admin audit record; decision events carry `GrantID`.
done_when: An agent can obtain a grant-bound token only after the user approves it in the portal, the worker blocks tools outside the grant, and revocation takes effect on the next bundle apply.

summary: The CP keeps a registry of approved MCP servers: transport, endpoint or command, owner team, versions, approved tool sets, schema pins and binary integrity. Changes are versioned with one-click rollback and go to workers in the signed bundle, so the gateway and `warden mcp` enforce one central list instead of local config.
design: Tables `mcp_servers` (id slug, name, transport `http|sse|stdio`, url, command, args, env placeholder names only, owner_team, current_version) and `mcp_server_versions` (server_id, version int, label, approved_tools, schema_pins map tool->sha256 of inputSchema, integrity {sha256, ed25519PublicKey, ed25519Signature}, created_by, approved_by, created_at).
Schema pin hash uses the same algorithm as `gateway.hashSchema` (sha256 hex of raw inputSchema) so observed inventory hashes from CP `mcpStore` can be imported directly.

REST: `GET/POST /api/mcp/servers`, `POST /api/mcp/servers/{id}/versions`, `POST /api/mcp/servers/{id}/rollback {version}`, `GET /api/mcp/servers/{id}/versions/{v}/diff`. Writes need editor role; widening (new tools, new URL/command, removed pin) goes through the Phase 2 approval gate.
Bundle gains `mcpRegistry: [{id, transport, url, command, args, approvedTools, schemaPins, integrity, version}]`; workers keep last-known-good on bad bundles.

Worker: gateway option `WithRegistry` adds findings `mcp_unregistered_server` and `mcp_unregistered_tool`, and registry pins override per-session baselines for drift; `warden mcp --server <id>` reads integrity from the registry before local `mcp.servers`.
done_when: An admin registers a server and approves its tools in the console, workers receive it in the signed bundle, and an unapproved tool or schema change is blocked in enforce mode; rollback restores the previous version fleet-wide.

summary: `warden admin-mcp` is an MCP server for operators' own AI assistants, with tools to explain a decision, query traffic, suggest and replay policy, and list agents. It authenticates to the CP with a scoped API key, is read-only by default, and never returns bodies or secrets.
design: The command is a thin MCP server that calls CP REST APIs; it has no direct DB access. Flags: `--transport stdio|http`, `--listen :7071`, `--cp-url`, `--api-key-env WARDEN_API_KEY` (default), `--allow-writes`.

Tools map to API key scopes: explain_decision -> `audit:read`; query_traffic -> `traffic:read`; list_agents -> `agents:read`; suggest_policy, replay_policy -> `policy:read`. The server lists only tools the key's scopes allow (checked via `GET /api/keys/self`).

explain_decision(event_uid | agent+domain+time) calls new CP `GET /api/explain` which loads the policy version active at the event time, re-runs `policy.NewEvaluator` and returns matched rule, identity, grant, hook and MCP findings.
query_traffic uses `EventFilter`/`AggregatedFilter` with typed filters (agent, sub, domain, decision, tool, since, limit<=500); no free-form SQL.

suggest_policy wraps `policybuilder.Build` + `FormatYAML`; replay_policy wraps `policyeval.Evaluate` on fleet events. The only write tool, create_policy_draft, needs `--allow-writes` and `policy:draft`; nothing can approve or publish.
HTTP mode serves Streamable HTTP at `/mcp` and requires the caller to present the same API key as Bearer; responses are size-capped (256 KB).
done_when: Claude Code connected to `warden admin-mcp` with a read-only key can explain a specific deny, query recent traffic and replay a candidate policy, and cannot change anything.

summary: Policy can live in Git: the CP pulls YAML from a repo into drafts that go through the same replay and approval gates as console edits, and CI can lint and replay changes before merge. Approved versions can be rolled out to a canary subset of workers, watched, then promoted or rolled back.
design: CP config `gitops: {repo, branch, path, interval: 60s, auth: {sshKeySecret|tokenSecret}, mode: advisory|authoritative}` using go-git (pure Go) pull only; CP never pushes. In authoritative mode console edits to policy are disabled.

New commit -> parse files under `path` with the normal config loader + validation -> create a draft with provenance {source: git, commit, author, message}; drafts then run replay via `policyeval.Evaluate` and the Phase 2 approval gate unchanged.

CLI for CI: `warden policy lint <file>` (strict YAML parse + validation, non-zero exit) and `warden policy replay --candidate f --cp-url --api-key-env` (remote replay against fleet events; `--fail-on-new-allows`).

Canary: `rollouts` table {id, version, targets (worker ids or percent), status canary|promoted|rolled_back, started_at}. `ServePolicy` picks the version per worker identity (mTLS SAN worker id), ETag per version.

Status from heartbeats (`policyETag` already reported) plus canary vs stable deny rate and error rate from the fleet store; promote sets current version for all; rollback returns canary workers to stable.
done_when: A merged policy PR appears as a draft with replay results, is approved, rolled out to a canary worker, and promoted or rolled back from the console with status visible per worker.

summary: The control plane can run on Postgres instead of SQLite and as multiple replicas behind a load balancer. Background jobs run on exactly one replica via advisory-lock leader election, and policy long-polls on any replica wake within a second of a change on another.
design: Store selection via `--store-provider sqlite|postgres` and `--postgres-dsn-env` (DSN read from env, never from config file); analytics.NewFleetStore's existing `postgres` branch (currently 'not yet implemented') returns a new FleetPostgresStore; all other CP stores (policy versions, block list, agent/MCP registries, sessions, worker tokens/certs, grants, API keys, admin audit index, alerts) get a Postgres implementation behind their existing interfaces.

Driver: jackc/pgx/v5 via database/sql (`pgx/v5/stdlib`); migrations as embedded, numbered SQL files per store run by a small migrator holding `pg_advisory_lock(hash('warden_migrate'))` so concurrent replicas migrate once; schema version table `warden_schema_migrations`.

Leader election: a dedicated connection holds `pg_try_advisory_lock(<job-key>)` per background job family (retention, offboarding refresh, git sync, detection tick, alert delivery, backups); loss of the connection drops leadership; jobs from p4-bg-jobs gain a `Leader` gate; SQLite mode keeps a no-op always-leader implementation.

Fan-out: policy/bundle publish does `NOTIFY warden_policy, '<version>'`; each replica runs a LISTEN loop that calls policyServer.Refresh/policyWatch.set so `/policy?wait=` and `/connect/{id}/status?wait=` waiters wake on all replicas; a 3s poll (existing policyReloadInterval) remains as a fallback when LISTEN reconnects.

The fleet Query Builder on Postgres runs in a `SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY` transaction with `statement_timeout`, against a restricted role, and Schema() reports dialect `postgres`; WorkerRegistry live state stays per-replica in memory but last-seen is upserted to a `workers` table so the dashboard shows the whole fleet.

`warden control-plane migrate-store --from sqlite:<state-dir> --to postgres` copies all stores in dependency order, verifies row counts and checksums, and refuses to run against a non-empty target unless `--force`.

summary: Token-signing, bundle-signing and worker-CA private keys can live in AWS KMS, GCP Cloud KMS or Vault transit instead of CP state. The CP signs through a Signer interface, and rotation creates a new KMS key version with the same overlap rules as local keys.

Backends: AWS KMS (`Sign` with ECDSA_SHA_256 on ECC_NIST_P256; Ed25519 not supported by AWS KMS so ES256 is required), GCP KMS (`asymmetricSign`, EC_SIGN_P256_SHA256 or EC_SIGN_ED25519), Vault transit (`/v1/transit/sign/<key>` with ed25519 or ecdsa-p256). Config per key purpose: `keys.{token,bundle,ca}.{backend: local|awskms|gcpkms|vault, keyRef, region, vaultAddr, authEnv}`; `kid` derived from key ARN/resource version so JWKS and bundle pins stay stable across restarts and replicas.

Worker-CA signing implements crypto.Signer over the KMS backend so x509.CreateCertificate works unchanged; bundle signing algorithm becomes negotiable (Ed25519 or ES256) with the algorithm recorded in the bundle header.

Rotation: `warden control-plane keys rotate --purpose token` creates/selects a new key version, publishes it in JWKS alongside the old one for the overlap window, then switches signing; failure to reach KMS fails issuance closed (no fallback to local key) and raises a self-monitoring alert.

design: New package `internal/identity`: `Claims{Sub, Email, Groups, SID, Issuer, Expiry}`, a `Verifier` interface `Verify(ctx, raw string) (Claims, error)`, and an OIDC implementation on `github.com/coreos/go-oidc/v3` RemoteKeySet (JWKS cached, refetched on unknown kid, at most one fetch per 30s). It checks iss, that aud contains the configured audience, exp/nbf with 60s skew, and an algorithm allowlist (RS256, ES256). A fake verifier lives in test/fakes.

Config is distributed in `SettingsWire.Identity{Mode, Issuer, Audience, PerAgent map[agentID]mode}` and applied by the SettingsApplier. Valid modes are `off|attribute`, and `require` fails validation with a 'Phase 2' error. The agent stays identified by port (`agentid.PortBindingIdentifier`).

Extraction: the `handleConn` header loop captures `Proxy-Authorization` (Basic user `session` -> token; Bearer also accepted). A new first request stage `identityStage` reads `X-Warden-Identity: Bearer`. Both headers are always deleted before forwarding, even in mode off. Failure in attribute mode: the request proceeds, `IdentityStatus` is set to `none|valid|invalid|expired`, and the metric `warden_identity_verify_total{result}` is incremented. The raw token is never logged, stored or passed to the judge.

Event gains `UserSub, UserEmail, UserGroups, UserSID, IdentityStatus`. These are additive SQLite columns on the local and fleet stores, flow through sync/ingest, and are covered by signed receipts automatically because `Signer.Sign` marshals the whole Event.

design: Per-agent settings `park: {enabled: false, maxWait: 20s (cap 60s), notify: true}` distributed in SettingsWire; worker-wide `park.maxConcurrent` (default 256) and `park.maxPerUser` (default 8). Overflow returns the JIT 403 immediately.

Worker calls CP `POST /internal/park` (worker mTLS) with {sub, agent, provider, scopes or grant request, method, host, path-without-query}; CP reuses or creates the pending authorization from p3-connect-links, sends the notification, and returns {authorization_id, status_url}.

New package internal/park: `Waiter.Wait(ctx, statusURL, deadline)` long-polls `GET /connect/{id}/status?wait=` until completed, denied or deadline. Effective deadline = min(maxWait, client hint `X-Warden-Max-Wait`, global cap).

On completion the worker invalidates the per-user token cache entry and re-runs the secret swap stage, then forwards. The request body stays in memory (already bounded by maxBodySwapSize) and is never persisted.

Client-gone safety: a watcher on the client conn aborts the park when the client closes; the request is never forwarded after abort. Metrics `warden_park_total{outcome}` (resumed|timeout|denied|client_gone|overflow) and `warden_park_wait_seconds`.
